## TL;DR

QA'd the first-run experience — Work with no tasks, Agents with no configured
roles, Checks with no check plan — headlessly at 375, 768 and 1280 px against
preview fixtures, using the repo's established `just serve-noauth` + WebKit
Playwright pattern. Two real defects found and fixed, both about an empty state
sending mixed signals: the Checks plan tab rendered a red "No plan configured"
chip plus a redundant red error paragraph right above the amber "this is fine
for now" reminder (#0592 says an error-free empty plan must never read as a
failure), and the mobile Work queue told a user with zero tasks "No matching
tasks" when nothing had been filtered. To make the Checks first-run state
reviewable at all I added a `checks:emptyPlan` preview fixture (there was no way
to capture a repo without a check plan). Layout was clean: zero overflow and
zero off-viewport controls on all three states at all three widths. All
first-run actions exercised headlessly and working.

## Work and rationale

- **New fixture `checks:emptyPlan`** (`src/core/shot-fixtures.ts`,
  `src/ui-app/src/lib/shot-preview-fixtures.ts`, consumed by
  `ChecksView.load()`): pins a genuinely empty, error-free plan (source
  `empty`, zero steps, no errors, no recorded run). Rationale: the preview
  board always reflects this repo's real committed check plan, so the
  first-run Checks page could not be seen or captured without editing
  `repoos.toml` — which the task forbids. The pin follows the existing
  `pinnedCheckRuns`/`pinnedIntegration` pattern and resets with the other
  pins.
- **Checks plan tab de-escalation** (`src/ui-app/src/views/ChecksView.vue`):
  the `data-source="empty"` chip is now neutral (`var(--txt-muted)`) instead
  of red; the trailing red paragraph is suppressed when the amber reminder is
  already shown (the genuinely empty case) and kept — reworded to "No check
  steps resolved for this repo." — for the odd zero-steps-without-errors plan
  whose source is not `empty`. I kept `repoos init` in that sentence after
  verifying `init.ts` really proposes a starter plan via `proposeCheckPlan`.
- **Mobile Work count line**
  (`src/ui-app/src/components/MobileWorkQueue.vue`): `countLabel` now
  distinguishes "No tasks yet" (board is empty — nothing to match) from
  "No matching tasks" (tasks exist, a filter hides them).
- **QA scripts committed** under `docs/qa/`:
  `measure-first-run-widths.mjs` (layout matrix, waits for each state's own
  selector to rule out the loading-skeleton race I hit on the first pass) and
  `first-run-interactions.mjs` (the first-run actions at 375/1280).
- **QA report** committed as `docs/qa/2026-11-first-run-qa.md` with the
  findings table, evidence and not-verified section.

## Approaches tried

- I first measured with a plain fixed wait (copied from the older
  `measure-mobile-widths.mjs`); the 768 Agents capture caught the loading
  skeleton instead of the first-run card because the model-refresh request
  was slow. Rather than only lengthening the wait, I made each route wait for
  its state's own selector (`[data-testid=agents-empty-state]`, `.mobile-queue-empty`,
  `.ncpr`) with a timeout, which both fixes the race and fails loudly when the
  state never renders.
- For the Checks fix I considered recolouring the red paragraph to amber
  instead of removing it, but the reminder directly above it already says the
  same thing in the right tone; keeping both would be duplication. Removing it
  only when `isGenuinelyEmptyPlan(plan)` preserves a call to action for the
  genuinely odd resolved-to-zero-steps case.
- Verified the docs links before touching anything: `docs.repoos.org/check`
  and `/agents` resolve, so the audit found no dead links to fix.

## Challenges and blockers

- The full local test suite is currently flaky in this environment for
  reasons unrelated to this diff, and I want that on record rather than
  hidden. Run 1: 10,148 passed, one failure — `preview-request.test.ts`
  timing out waiting for a preview-ready transcript entry under load; it
  passes in isolation (12/12, 13 s). Run 2 (after I stopped the QA server):
  748 files failed at the import level with a single environmental signature
  (`ENOENT` inside this runner session's `~/.repoos/agent-run-tmp` TMPDIR, plus
  a `posix_spawn 'git'` ENOENT), zero assertion failures. The machine is under
  memory pressure (12.2 of 13.3 GB swap used; `repoos stats` reports pressure
  "warning — advisory only"), which the repo documents as a real flake class.
  Every touched test file passes repeatedly in isolation, and the scoped
  `repoos check` is fully green — its test step ran on the remote validation
  runner, per the gate's own configuration. I did not chase the environmental
  failures further per `docs/debugging-check-failures.md`.
- The scoped check caught two formatting lints in my new files
  (`bun run fmt` fixed them); the `--changed main` run then passed every step
  including the rendered contrast audit.

## Key learnings

- Empty states drift into alarm-colour. The Checks page had been fixed once
  (#0592) to stop rendering a skipped gate as green, but the same state still
  carried red "failure" styling in two other places on the same screen — a
  reminder that a colour-policy decision has to be applied at the state level,
  not per element. The new test pins the whole shape (reminder present, zero
  `.ck-err` lines) rather than one selector.
- "No matching tasks" vs "No tasks yet" is the same lesson in words: an empty
  result set from a filter and an empty project are different user moments
  with different next actions. The desktop board already had this right; the
  mobile count line did not.
- A QA pass that can't reach the state it's auditing will quietly audit
  nothing. The missing `checks:emptyPlan` fixture was the real blocker for
  this task's acceptance criteria; building the fixture first made every other
  check meaningful and left the state capturable for future reviews.
